tracks.title: From messy data to your first model
tracks.description: Clean a real-shaped dataset, build a leakage-safe pipeline, and measure what your model actually learns.
tracks.prerequisites: Basic Python. No ML experience required.

steps.title: Inspect and clean data
steps.outcome: A CSV quality report with row counts, invalid dates, and missing amounts.
steps.challenge: Add a check for duplicate order IDs. Explain why dropping every incomplete row can bias your dataset.

steps.title: Train a tabular pipeline
steps.outcome: outputs/03-sklearn-precision-recall.png and .svg, plus a classification report.
steps.challenge: Compare average precision with the printed prevalence baseline. Change the split seed and explain the variation.

tracks.title: Build and debug a neural network
tracks.description: Follow tensors through autograd, train a nonlinear classifier, and inspect learning curves on your CPU.
tracks.prerequisites: Python arrays and basic train/test splits. Complete ML foundations first if these are new.

steps.title: Learn tensors and autograd
steps.outcome: outputs/01-tensors-autograd.png showing regression fit, loss, parameters, and gradients.
steps.challenge: Double the learning rate. Does the loss still converge? Compare the learned slope and intercept with the target.

steps.title: Train a nonlinear classifier
steps.outcome: outputs/02-mlp-classification.png with decision boundaries and test accuracy.
steps.challenge: Reduce the hidden layer size. Compare test accuracy and training loss, and identify signs of underfitting.

tracks.title: Prepare images for machine learning
tracks.description: Build a visual preprocessing workflow: preserve geometry, inspect transformations, and understand what filters remove.
tracks.prerequisites: Basic Python. No GPU or deep learning framework required.

steps.title: Resize without distorting geometry
steps.outcome: outputs/01-resize-comparison.png comparing resize, crop, and thumbnail operations.
steps.challenge: Choose a target aspect ratio for an image classifier. Explain which transformation preserves the important features.

steps.title: Compare enhancements and filters
steps.outcome: outputs/02-enhancement-grid.png comparing contrast, blur, sharpness, and edge filters.
steps.challenge: Increase blur and compare fine details. Describe when preprocessing would remove information needed by the model.

tracks.title: Run MLX on your Mac
tracks.description: Train with autograd and measure compiled execution using MLX on Apple silicon. Start small, inspect outputs, and choose the CPU or Metal GPU.
tracks.prerequisites: An Apple silicon Mac running macOS 14+ with native arm64 Python 3.11–3.13. Basic Python arrays and gradients.

steps.title: Train with MLX autograd
steps.outcome: outputs/mlx-autograd.json with the selected device, falling loss, and learned slope near 2.5 and intercept near -0.8.
steps.challenge: Change the learning rate in labs/lab01_mlx_autograd.py. Compare the final loss and learned parameters, then retry with --device cpu.

steps.title: Measure compiled execution
steps.outcome: outputs/mlx-compile.json with output agreement, warm execution medians, and an observed timing ratio on your selected device.
steps.challenge: Change the input shape in labs/lab02_mlx_compile.py. Compare warm timings on CPU and Metal separately. Explain why compilation is not always faster.
